answer: A public canyon admits one 36-second probe at a time, blocking parallel clones. The key writes its payer into a write-once basalt column and parks 2,280 POA idle for 18 epochs. On call it opens a one-shot lotus, a 44-byte reveal bound to that row; two auditors replay it before the next probe. Late, copied, or second columns from the same payer burn 590 POA and seal the row 16 epochs. One key idles 2,280 POA plus 36s; 900 fakes need 2.052 million POA and nine exclusive hours, vs ~150 POA. Farms may dribble keys over epochs; refuse a second lotus from any payer within two hops and slash both.
